messages:
Mira Chen: quick sync — proposing a formal parity-bench protocol for model comparisons (same prompts, identical decode params, tokenizer alignment, and replay harness semantics). want to lock this down before we run the big suite.
Jonas Patel: +1. do you mean we canonicalize tokenization (single tokenizer implementation) or allow model-native tokenizers but compare at token boundaries?
Mira Chen: prefer canonicalization. model-native tokenizers cause off-by-one tokenization differences that break stop-sequence parity. plan: store raw utf8 prompt text in the replay logs, then run a single tokenizer implementation (tokenizer-sync) to generate the token stream we feed to each model runtime.
Priya Rao: that matches my concerns. also need deterministic stop handling: if stop sequence splits across stream chunks we should apply the same detection logic in post-processing, not rely on model truncation heuristics.
Liam ONeill: noted. batching also affects decoding timing — the batcher needs to reserve slots deterministically for identical decode steps. otherwise latency comparisons are noisy. proposal: use fixed micro-batch schedule in the harness (no dynamic coalescing).
Mira Chen: exactly. harness config example:
```json
{
  "replay_input": "prompts.parquet",
  "tokenizer_impl": "tokenizer-sync.py",
  "decode": {"temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 0.95, "max_tokens": 128, "stop": ["\n\n"]},
  "batching_policy": "fixed_microbatch_v1",
  "kv_warmup": true
}
```
Jonas Patel: small nit — kv_warmup true needs to be explicit about policy: prefill vs. on-demand prefetch. i recommend two phases: (1) kv-prefill from cached prefix tokens, (2) measured real-time streaming with cold/warm runs.
Danielle Kim: for kernel selection tests we should surface the kernel predicate decisions per step in the trace. otherwise we can't map perf deltas to kernel mismatch. add `kernel_trace: true` to the run.
Mira Chen: good call. also add `kernels_snapshot` to capture the selected kernel id + dispatch args for each iteration. we saw a perf regression where the predicate flipped to a slow path for length>64.
Priya Rao: what metrics do we capture? p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU SM utilization, memory transient, kernel occupancy, and KV hit-rate. also capture scheduler queue length and batch sizes observed.
Liam ONeill: add `decode_steps_per_second` and `kv_prefetch_latency_ms`. and sample a per-token profile for the first 50 tokens to spot warmup cliffs.
infra-bot: deploy recorded: replay-harness/2026-03-15T12:03Z -> compute-cluster/staging (sha: a1b2c3).
eval-bot: new result available: runs/1765432100-tokenizer-sync/seed-42 (summary uploaded to /runs/1765432100/summary.json).
Jonas Patel: saw the summary — modelB p95 is +22% vs modelA on mixed prompt set. raw trace shows kernel flip at token 67 and batch collapse from 8->3. that matches the slowdown.
Mira Chen: action items: 1) add kernel_trace & kernels_snapshot full time-series to harness (Priya) 2) add deterministic tokenizer-sync and stop-postprocess (Jonas) 3) run cold vs warm KV prefill comparison (Liam) 4) re-run the 4k-prompt suite with fixed_microbatch_v1 (Danielle).
Danielle Kim: I'll kick off the re-run after I add a small shim to log kernel IDs into the perf trace recorder. ETA 2hrs.
Priya Rao: for reproducibility include the exact git sha of tokenizer-sync, kernel commit, and runtime build id in the run metadata. also store the full docker image digest.
Mira Chen: agreed. last thing: when writing the paper/notes, call this "parity-bench protocol" and include an appendix with the exact harness command we used. sample command to run locally: 
```bash
./bin/replay_harness \
  --prompts prompts.parquet \
  --tokenizer ./tokenizer-sync.py \
  --models "/runs/modelA:/runs/modelB" \
  --decode '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":0.95,"max_tokens":128,"stop":["\\n\\n"]}' \
  --batching fixed_microbatch_v1 \
  --kernel-trace true \
  --kv-warmup prefill \
  --outdir /tmp/parity_run_1765432100
```
Jonas Patel: perfect. also add a tiny regression test: if two models produce different tokenized sequences for the same prompt under tokenizer-sync, fail the run and dump diffs.
Mira Chen: yes — fail fast. I'll draft the README for the protocol and the checklist (metadata included) and post it in this channel when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
Priya Rao: thanks — excited to finally have a defensible way to compare models without tokenization or batching noise.
Liam ONeill: I'll instrument KV prefill paths to record prefetch latency distribution.
Danielle Kim: starting runs now, will report back with the first heatmap and p95 table.
Mira Chen: awesome. closing loop later today.
